statement: A bike lock opens with a $3$-digit code, where each digit is one of $0$ through $9$. Jada wants a code whose first digit is odd, whose last digit is even, and whose three digits are all different. How many codes can she choose from?

choices.misconception: I forgot that 0 is an even digit, so I gave the last digit only 4 choices: 5 x 4 x 8 = 160.
I did not let the middle digit be 0, so it had only 7 choices: 5 x 5 x 7 = 175.
I counted 720 codes with three different digits and assumed exactly a quarter of them start odd and end even.
I only made the middle digit different from the first digit, so it had 9 choices: 5 x 5 x 9 = 225.

hints: Choose the digits with the most restrictions first.
The first digit has $5$ odd choices and the last digit has $5$ even choices. Can those two ever be equal?
An odd digit and an even digit are always different, so the middle digit just has to avoid those $2$ digits.

solutions.reliable: Choose the first digit from $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$ ($5$ ways) and the last digit from $0, 2, 4, 6, 8$ ($5$ ways). These are automatically different, since one is odd and one is even. The middle digit must differ from both, leaving $10 - 2 = 8$ choices. The total is $5 \times 5 \times 8 = 200$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
